title: The Great Depression
objective: After this level you can explain what caused the Great Depression and how it changed economic policy.
summary: From 1929, US output fell by a third and prices fell. Economists still debate the cause (the crash, a shrinking money supply, the gold standard). It reshaped economic policy.

cards.headline: In 2002, a Fed official apologized for the Great Depression.
cards.body: At a conference honoring Milton Friedman, Ben Bernanke told Friedman and Anna Schwartz: "Regarding the Great Depression. You're right, we did it. We're very sorry." Not every economist agrees on who "did it".

cards.fact: Between 1929 and 1933, US output fell by about a third.
cards.context: Unemployment reached about 25% of the labor force, and thousands of banks failed, more than 1,000 a year from 1930 to 1933. Prices fell about 10% a year: Level 64's deflation at full strength. The slump lasted until about 1941, the longest and deepest downturn in US history.

cards.headline: Who did it? Economists still argue
cards.body: Economists still disagree about the cause. One story starts with the 1929 stock market crash, which destroyed wealth and scared consumers and firms into spending less. Milton Friedman and Anna Schwartz blamed a shrinking money supply: as banks failed and the Fed failed to step in, money fell by nearly 30%, and spending fell with it. Others stress Level 7's gold standard, which helped spread the slump from country to country.

cards.headline: The Depression rewrote the rulebook
cards.body: The Depression sparked fundamental changes in economic institutions, policy and theory. The US got federal deposit insurance, securities regulation, Social Security and its first national minimum wage. And the Fed took the lesson personally: Bernanke's apology ended, "But thanks to you, we won't do it again."

cards.headline: Great Depression: explained
learned: 1929 to about 1941: the deepest US downturn
Output fell by a third; unemployment hit 25%; prices fell
Causes still debated: crash, money supply, gold standard
It brought deposit insurance, Social Security and more

questions.prompt: Between 1929 and 1933, roughly how much did US output fall?

options.label: About a tenth
options.rationale: The fall was far deeper: about a third.

options.label: About a half
options.rationale: Close, but the fall was about a third.

options.label: About nine-tenths
options.rationale: That would mean almost nothing was produced.

questions.explanation: US output fell by about a third between 1929 and 1933, while unemployment reached about 25%.

questions.prompt: In Friedman and Schwartz's account, how did bank failures deepen the Depression?

options.label: Banks raised prices on everything they sold
options.rationale: Banks don't set shop prices; the money supply was the issue.

options.label: Failed banks bought up too many factories
Bank failures pushed interest rates to zero
options.rationale: Their story is about money shrinking.

options.label: The money supply shrank, so spending fell

questions.explanation: As banks failed and the Fed failed to step in, the money supply fell by nearly 30% and spending fell with it.

questions.prompt: The Depression gave the US federal deposit insurance. From Level 29, what was the FDIC created to protect?

options.label: Stock prices on Wall Street
options.rationale: Securities rules were a separate change.

options.label: Workers' pay through a minimum wage
options.rationale: The minimum wage was another reform, not the FDIC's job.

questions.explanation: Created in 1933 after thousands of bank failures, the FDIC exists to keep public confidence in banks, the answer to runs.
